name: saussuritised
description: Hydrothermal alteration of plagioclase feldspar into a fine-grained assemblage of zoisite, epidote, albite, calcite, and sericite.

name: serpentinisation
description: Hydration and metamorphic transformation of ultramafic rocks, converting olivine and pyroxene into serpentine minerals.

name: epidote alteration
description: Replacement of primary rock minerals, typically plagioclase or mafic minerals, by epidote.

name: silicification
description: Introduction of, or replacement by, silica (quartz, chalcedony, or opal) into the rock.

name: carbonate alteration
description: Introduction of carbonate minerals such as calcite, dolomite, ankerite, or siderite into a rock.

name: calcsilicate alteration
description: Formation of calcium-bearing silicate minerals, such as garnet and pyroxene, often in skarn or contact metamorphic environments.

name: greisen
description: Pneumatolytic alteration of granitic rock characterized by the formation of quartz, muscovite, and halogen-bearing minerals like topaz and fluorite.

name: albitic alteration
description: Sodium metasomatism resulting in the replacement of K-feldspar or calcic plagioclase by albite.

name: advanced argillic alteration
description: Intense acidic hydrothermal alteration characterized by the leaching of alkalis and the formation of kaolinite, dickite, pyrophyllite, and alunite.

name: not altered
description: Rock or sediment not altered.

name: chloritic alteration
description: Replacement of primary mafic minerals (like pyroxene or biotite) or glassy matrix by chlorite.

name: zeolitic alteration
description: Low-temperature hydrothermal alteration or diagenesis resulting in the formation of zeolite minerals.

name: propylitic alteration
description: Low-temperature, low-to-medium grade alteration characterized by the assemblage of chlorite, epidote, calcite, and albite.

name: potassic alteration
description: High-temperature alteration characterized by the introduction of potassium, forming secondary K-feldspar and/or biotite.

name: alteration type not specified
description: Rock is altered, but type not specified. Any alteration type allowed.

name: kaolinitic alteration
description: Hydrothermal alteration or severe weathering producing kaolinite group minerals, typically from the breakdown of feldspars.

name: sericitic alteration
description: Phyllic alteration characterized by the breakdown of feldspars into fine-grained white mica (sericite) and quartz, often with pyrite.

name: argillic alteration
description: Hydrothermal alteration forming clay minerals such as smectite and illite, typically representing lower temperatures or less acidic conditions than advanced argillic.

name: alunitic alteration
description: A specific type of advanced argillic alteration dominated by the sulfate mineral alunite, indicating highly acidic and oxidizing conditions.

name: hematitic alteration
description: Oxidation of iron-bearing minerals to form hematite, often giving rocks a distinctive red or reddish-brown color.

name: pyritic alteration
description: Introduction of pyrite into a rock, typically as a result of sulfur-rich hydrothermal fluids reacting with iron-bearing minerals.

name: deuteric alteration
description: Late-stage magmatic alteration where the residual fluids from a crystallizing magma alter the early-formed minerals within the same igneous body.

name: uralitisation
description: Late-magmatic or metamorphic alteration of primary pyroxene into fibrous amphibole (actinolite-tremolite series).

name: red rock alteration
description: Widespread hematite dusting or staining of feldspars, often associated with oxidized, saline hydrothermal fluids.
